stages.name: Tribes and kingdoms
stages.desc: Thracians, Illyrians, Scythians, Getae and Colchians, with Greek ports on their coasts

stages.name: Free Greek cities
stages.desc: Self-governing city-states: Athens, Corinth, Sparta, Thebes

stages.name: Persian Empire
stages.desc: Lands of the Great King, ruled by his satraps

stages.name: Kingdom of Macedon
stages.desc: Philip II's kingdom and the lands he annexed

stages.name: Greece under Macedon
stages.desc: Cities bound to Macedon by the League of Corinth

stages.name: Alexander's conquests
stages.desc: Former Persian lands won by Alexander

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: Greek and Phoenician kings rule Cyprus's cities as subjects of Persia
Evagoras of Salamis wages a ten-year war against Persia
Zeno of Citium, the future founder of Stoicism, is born about now
The kings of Cyprus bring their ships over to Alexander at Tyre

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Phoenician cities, Tyre and Sidon, provide Persia's fleet
Alexander takes Tyre after a seven-month siege

states.name: Syria
timeline: The Persian satrapy 'Beyond the River'
After Issus, Alexander's general takes Damascus

states.name: Ukraine
timeline: Scythian steppe; Greek ports at Olbia and Chersonesus

states.name: Georgia
timeline: Colchis, with Greek trading posts such as Phasis

states.name: North Macedonia
timeline: Paeonians and upland peoples north of Macedon
Philip II subdues the Paeonians

states.name: Albania
timeline: Illyrian tribes inland; Greek colonies at Epidamnus and Apollonia on the coast
Philip II of Macedon defeats the Illyrian king Bardylis

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Persian satraps rule Anatolia; Greek ports such as Sinope run their own affairs
The King's Peace hands the Greek cities of Asia to Persia
Alexander's victory at the Granicus opens Anatolia

states.name: Armenia
timeline: The Persian satrapy of Armenia
After Gaugamela, Alexander names his own satrap of Armenia

states.name: Romania
timeline: Getae north of the Danube; Greek ports at Histria, Tomis and Callatis
Philip defeats the Scythian king Ateas near the Danube
Alexander crosses the Danube against the Getae

states.name: Greece
timeline: Self-governing cities at war: Athens against Sparta and Corinth; Macedon's kings rule the north
Athens surrenders; Sparta dominates Greece
Thebes breaks Sparta's power at Leuctra
Philip defeats Athens and Thebes at Chaeronea
The League of Corinth binds the cities to Macedon
Alexander destroys rebellious Thebes

states.name: Bulgaria
timeline: The Odrysian kingdom of Thrace; Greek ports along the Black Sea coast
Philip conquers Thrace and founds Philippopolis

states.name: Moldova
timeline: Getae and Scythian lands between the Dniester and the Prut

events.title: Born in Sinope
events.text: Diogenes, son of the banker Hicesias, is born about now, or a few years later, in a Greek port on the Black Sea.

events.title: Persia returns west
events.text: Persian satraps back Sparta with money to retake the Greek cities of Asia from Athens.

events.title: Aegospotami
events.text: Sparta's fleet destroys Athens' navy in the Hellespont.

events.title: Athens surrenders
events.text: Starved by blockade, Athens pulls down its Long Walls.

events.title: Ten Thousand at Sinope
events.text: Greek mercenaries retreating from Persia reach Sinope's coast and sail on from its harbour.

events.title: Socrates executed
events.text: Athens condemns Socrates to death for impiety and corrupting the young.

events.title: Evagoras' war
events.text: Evagoras, king of Salamis on Cyprus, begins a ten-year war against Persia.

events.title: King's Peace
events.text: At Sardis, a Persian satrap reads out the Great King's terms: the Greek cities of Asia are his.

events.title: Plato's Academy
events.text: Plato begins teaching in the Academy, a grove outside Athens' walls.

events.title: Leuctra
events.text: Thebes defeats Sparta and ends its rule over Greece.

events.title: Persian coins at Sinope
events.text: Sinope's mint strikes silver for the Persian satrap Datames: the nymph Sinope and a sea-eagle on a dolphin.

events.title: Antisthenes teaches
events.text: The aged Socratic Antisthenes teaches at the Cynosarges gymnasium; he dies around 365.

events.title: Mantinea
events.text: Thebes' general Epaminondas wins and dies; no Greek city is left strong enough to lead.

events.title: Philip becomes king
events.text: Philip II takes the throne of Macedon and rebuilds its army.

events.title: Amphipolis taken
events.text: Philip seizes Amphipolis and the gold mines of Mount Pangaion.

events.title: Alexander born
events.text: Philip's son Alexander is born at Pella.

events.title: The coinage scandal
events.text: At a disputed date, from the 360s to the 340s, Sinope's coins are defaced and Diogenes goes into exile.

events.title: The oracle
events.text: One version: Apollo's oracle tells him to alter the currency, and he takes it literally.

events.title: Into Athens
events.text: The exile reaches Athens with a cloak, a staff and a beggar's wallet.

events.title: The jar
events.text: He makes his home in a great clay storage jar by the Metroon, in the Agora.

events.title: Philip wins Thessaly
events.text: At the Crocus Field Philip defeats the Phocians and becomes master of Thessaly.

events.title: Lamp in daylight
events.text: A story: he walks the Agora at noon with a lit lamp, 'looking for a man'.

events.title: Plato's man
events.text: A story: he brings a plucked chicken to the Academy: 'Here is Plato's man.'

events.title: Olynthus destroyed
events.text: Philip razes Olynthus and sells its people into slavery.

events.title: Plato dies
events.text: Plato dies in Athens, aged about eighty.

events.title: Taken by pirates
events.text: At an unknown date, a story says, pirates seize him on a voyage to Aegina.

events.title: Sold in Crete
events.text: Put up for sale, he says his trade is governing men; a Corinthian, Xeniades, buys him.

events.title: Tutor in Corinth
events.text: Xeniades sets him over his sons and household in Corinth.

events.title: Aristotle at Mieza
events.text: Aristotle becomes tutor to the thirteen-year-old Alexander.

events.title: Thrace conquered
events.text: Philip conquers the Thracian kingdom and founds Philippopolis.

events.title: Byzantium resists
events.text: Byzantium, helped by Athens, holds out against Philip's siege.

events.title: Chaeronea
events.text: Philip and the eighteen-year-old Alexander defeat Athens and Thebes.

events.title: A spy on greed
events.text: One account: Diogenes, captured, is brought to Philip and calls himself 'a spy upon your greed'.

events.title: League of Corinth
events.text: The Greek cities meet at Corinth and bind themselves to Philip for a war on Persia.

events.title: Philip murdered
events.text: Philip is stabbed at Aegae; Alexander, twenty, becomes king.

events.title: Out of my sun
events.text: Legend: Alexander finds Diogenes in the Craneum; 'Stand a little out of my sun.'

events.title: Thebes destroyed
events.text: Alexander razes Thebes, home of Diogenes' future pupil Crates.

events.title: Aristotle's Lyceum
events.text: Aristotle returns to Athens and opens his school at the Lyceum.

events.title: Granicus
events.text: Alexander crosses into Asia and defeats the Persian satraps.

events.title: Zeno is born
events.text: Zeno, who will found the Stoics, is born about now at Citium on Cyprus.

events.title: Issus
events.text: Alexander defeats the Persian king Darius III.

events.title: Tyre falls
events.text: After seven months, Alexander's army storms the island city of Tyre.

events.title: Crates' fortune
events.text: About now, Crates of Thebes gives away his fortune to live as Diogenes' pupil.

events.title: Death in Corinth
events.text: Diogenes dies nearly ninety; legend says on the day Alexander died in Babylon.

events.title: The marble dog
events.text: He is buried by the gate to the Isthmus, under a pillar topped by a marble dog.

eras: The end of the Peloponnesian War
chartNote: Share of the area of the thirteen present-day countries on the map, by the power that ruled most of each. A simplification: Greece shows its free southern cities, though Macedon's homeland lay in today's northern Greece; Turkey shows Persia, though Sinope and other Greek ports ran their own affairs; North Macedonia is mostly ancient Paeonia; and the large steppe lands swing the shares. Regions are today's boundaries; dates of Diogenes' own life are approximate and often disputed.
